quote: In 1694 he issued a solution's book to a collection of exercises by Heinrich Meißner, and later he published his own collection of 574 exercises from mathematics and astronomy, entitled Mathematischer Sinnen-Confect. In particular, exercise 289 on page 256 consists in finding the smallest Euler brick.
note: Paul Halcke published his mathematical collection (Mathematischer Sinnen-Confect) in 1694, which contained exercise 289 regarding Euler bricks—the precursor to the perfect cuboid problem. Halcke later found the first Euler brick in 1719 (sides 44, 117, 240). The perfect cuboid problem—asking whether a cuboid with integer edges, face diagonals, AND space diagonal exists—appears to have developed from his work on Euler bricks, though the exact year of first formal posing of the perfect cuboid problem is not definitively documented in standard references.
